rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable meningitis after a seizure/fit
rule_level_problems.problem: Evidence is Seizure AND (temperature >= 38 OR headache OR stiff neck OR purpuric rash). Headache is a recorded common symptom, so any seizure patient with a headache is diagnosed with probable meningitis and referred as Urgent. That is the literal reading of the 'any of' box, but 'meningitis likely' on headache alone is clinically loose; the builders should record the reading as a decision for a clinician.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: same-day referral after a seizure/fit
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Alcohol/drug use: overdose' is encoded only as Overdose (disorder). Alcohol intoxication (disorder) is not a descendant of Overdose (Overdose is under Poisoning), so alcohol overdose after a fit does not trigger referral. Add (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Alcohol intoxication" "disorder")) to the check_for and the or-list.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stroke from focal signs (seizure/fit page) / Diagnose probable TIA from focal signs (seizure/fit page)
rule_level_problems.problem: The page reaches 'Stroke or TIA likely' only on the 'did not have a seizure' branch; the rules fire on any focal sign regardless of context, including a patient who did have a seizure (where the same signs are red-box referral criteria and may be post-ictal). Defensible, since the signs warrant the diagnosis anyway, but the flowchart branch is not preserved.

Two of the page's discriminators are absent: twitching lasting < 15 seconds (not representable) and rapid recovery (no concept found; a (no Post-ictal state) conjunct would approximate it). Without them the rule can label a brief seizure with a prodrome as a faint.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: same-day referral after a seizure/fit
rule_level_problems.problem: Glucose is measured as (snomed_concept "Blood glucose status" "observable entity"). SNOMED also has "Blood glucose concentration" (observable entity); I could not verify which concept the routine glucose vital records under, and if it differs the three glucose criteria never fire. Builders should confirm against the vitals definition.

No possible Epilepsy rule for the page's 'doctor to consider epilepsy' (>= 2 definite seizures with no identifiable cause); the count is not representable, so this is a judgment call rather than a clear miss.

summary: The red box is encoded almost completely and accurately: all thresholds, units, time conditions and the HIV/no-epilepsy, diabetes and postpartum gates are right, every SNOMED concept exists, and every check_for item is consumed. The most consequential issues are (1) the probable-meningitis rule fires on seizure plus headache alone, which follows the box literally but will label many patients, and (2) alcohol overdose is not covered because Alcohol intoxication is not under Overdose. Lesser gaps: 'different' headache, the faint's duration and rapid-recovery discriminators, and no possible-epilepsy rule for 'consider epilepsy'.
